name: Process incoming e-invoices (XRechnung, ZUGFeRD) with IBAN fraud check, approval via email/WhatsApp/Telegram and DATEV forwarding

parameters.content:
## Process incoming e-invoices (XRechnung, ZUGFeRD, Factur-X, Peppol) — no data leaves your n8n

Since January 2025 every business in Germany has to be able to **receive** e-invoices, and from 2027/2028 B2B e-invoicing becomes mandatory. France, Belgium and others follow the same EN 16931 standard. The problem: an XRechnung is an XML file nobody can read, and a ZUGFeRD PDF hides its data in an attachment.

This workflow turns every incoming e-invoice into a clean, checked record — **without any external API, OCR service or community node**. The XML is read inside n8n with plain JavaScript, so invoice data stays on your instance (GDPR / DSGVO friendly).

### How it works
1. **Email (IMAP)** or the **upload form** delivers the files. PDF and XML are recognised by content (also without a file extension), **ZIP archives are unpacked**. A mail without any invoice file — typically a link to a supplier portal — is reported to accounting with the links found, instead of disappearing.
2. **Find e-invoice XML** takes XML files as they are and extracts the embedded XML from ZUGFeRD / Factur-X PDFs (PDF/A-3, decompressed in pure JS).
3. **Parse & check** reads CII (ZUGFeRD 2.x, Factur-X, XRechnung CII), ZUGFeRD 1.0 and UBL (XRechnung UBL, Peppol) into one structure and runs plausibility checks: line sums, net + VAT = gross, VAT per rate, amount due, IBAN checksum, VAT ID format, missing mandatory fields, overdue date.
4. PDFs **without** XML go to a **local AI model (Ollama)**, which reads the key fields. These are always marked for review. Scans without a text layer, broken PDFs and an unreachable model go straight to a person — nothing is lost when a step fails.
5. **Duplicates** (same seller + invoice number, or the identical file) are detected with an n8n Data Table, new invoices are stored there.
6. **Supplier check** against earlier invoices: an IBAN this supplier never used before stops the invoice (changed bank details are the classic invoice fraud), a different sender domain and a first invoice from a new supplier are noted.
7. Anything that needs attention — problems, AI-read PDFs, duplicates — is emailed to accounting, with a **readable PDF** of every XRechnung attached.
8. Clean invoices can be forwarded automatically to your bookkeeping inbox (**DATEV Upload Mail**, Lexware Office, …). DATEV Upload Mail does not accept XML, so XRechnungen are sent as the readable PDF.
9. *Export last month* sends a CSV of all invoices to your tax advisor.

Tested against the official ZUGFeRD / Factur-X corpus and the KoSIT XRechnung test suite (330 files) and end-to-end on n8n 2.43: IMAP trigger, Data Table, AI fallback, plus ten failure cases (changed IBAN, ZIP, portal link, scan, model down, same file name, non-invoice XML, duplicate). This is a plausibility check, not a full Schematron validation.

### Set up (about 10 minutes)
1. Run *Run once: create table* (yellow note) to create the **e_invoices** Data Table.
2. Add your **IMAP** credentials to *New invoice email* and **SMTP** credentials to the email nodes. Some hosts (e.g. DigitalOcean) block outgoing SMTP — then swap the email nodes for the Gmail or Microsoft Outlook node; attachment names work the same way.
3. Set your addresses in **Settings**. `accountingInbox` is optional: leave it empty to skip forwarding.
4. Optional: point *Local AI model* to your Ollama server (or swap in any chat model). If you don't need the PDF fallback, delete the purple section.
5. Test with the upload form, then activate.

Built by Denis Shokhirev · DennisCraft AI Studio, Freiburg — gerdennisai.com

### Data Table `e_invoices`
Click **Execute workflow** on *Run once: create table* — it creates the table with all columns.

`status` is **ok** or **check**, `source` is **e-invoice** or **pdf-ai**. Export the table as CSV for your accountant or DATEV import, or connect your accounting tool after the *Save invoice* node.

### Fallback: PDF without e-invoice data
Many suppliers still send plain PDFs. Their text goes to a **local** model via Ollama, so the invoice never leaves your infrastructure. Any chat model works (Mistral, Llama, Qwen — or a cloud model if your privacy rules allow it).

Scanned PDFs without a text layer, broken PDFs and a model that does not answer end up in *Could not read PDF* and are sent to a person with the file — add OCR in front if you get many scans.

### What is checked
- mandatory fields: number, date, seller, buyer, currency, totals
- sum of lines = line total, net + VAT = gross, VAT amount per rate, VAT breakdown = VAT total, amount due
- IBAN checksum (mod 97), VAT ID format
- warnings: credit note, due date passed, seller without VAT ID / tax number

### Supplier check — changed bank details
Fraudsters send a perfect copy of a real invoice with **their** IBAN. *Check supplier* compares every new invoice with the earlier ones of the same seller (VAT ID, else name):
- **IBAN never used by this supplier** → status *check*, with the advice to confirm by phone on a number you already know.
- different sender domain (e.g. `.de` → `.com`) and first invoice from a new supplier → note.

A new IBAN only becomes trusted when you set `ibanConfirmed` = `yes` on that row — an invoice that came in with the alarm never whitelists itself.

### Monthly export for your tax advisor
Run manually or swap the trigger for a *Schedule* (e.g. on the 2nd of every month). Sends last month's invoices as CSV (semicolon, decimal comma — opens directly in German Excel). Set the tax advisor's address in the last node.

parameters.content:
### Approval before payment — e-mail, WhatsApp or Telegram
Clean invoices from `approvalFromAmount` upwards (and every invoice not in `approvalCurrency`) are sent to the approver one by one, with **Freigeben / Ablehnen** buttons. Pick the channel in **Settings** → `approvalChannel`: `email` (works everywhere), `whatsapp` (WhatsApp Business Cloud), `telegram` or `none`.

Only approved invoices go on to the bookkeeping inbox; the decision is stored in the table. **No answer within `approvalWaitHours`** → accounting gets a mail, nothing waits forever. Note for WhatsApp: a free-text message is only delivered if the approver wrote to your business number within the last 24 hours — otherwise the request runs into this timeout.

parameters.content:
### When something fails
Email and Data Table steps retry 3× (5 s apart). If a step still fails, **On workflow error** sends accounting a mail with the step, the error and a link to the execution — because IMAP has already marked those mails as read, nothing would show up otherwise.

**One-time setup:** activate the workflow first (n8n only offers published workflows), then open *Workflow settings* → **Error workflow** → select **this** workflow, and set `accountingEmail` + `senderEmail` in *Failure settings*. (If SMTP itself is down, n8n's execution list still shows the failure.)
